correctness.rationale: Properness means that a class meeting both sides is precisely one missing matched pair: there is no third vertex nonadjacent to both endpoints. A class confined to one side is seen in full by an unmatched opposite vertex, hence has odd size. If it meets a matched endpoint, the matched opposite vertex sees one fewer, an even count which must vanish, so that class is a singleton. Conversely an unmatched-side odd block is seen in full or not at all; a matched singleton or pair is seen in at most one vertex, so the three types suffice independently. Fusing j of t pairs and partitioning the two unmatched sets gives 2t−j+k+l distinguishable blocks, assigned distinct named colors by the falling factorial. Odd-block partitions have EGF (sinh z)^k/k!, including the empty convention. Minimum block counts on positive odd and even sets are 1 and 2 respectively. A minimum forces all matched pairs fused; the number of optimal partitions from a positive even unmatched side is half the number of odd subsets, 2^(m−2). Multiplying the two counts and permuting the full optimum palette gives the stated multiplicity. The graph with t=0 and the one-edge deletion give the stated 4→3 and 2→5 changes. Saturation is genuinely excluded: in K2,2 minus a perfect matching two vertices on one side can share a color even though both are matched. An independent exact-cover enumeration using adjacency and all compatible subsets checked the whole block-count histogram and optima in 30 asymmetric cases with a+b≤10.
residual_risks: The independent replay is finite; necessity and sufficiency in the proof justify the full range. Neither the classification nor the formula is asserted for saturated sides or arbitrary cross-edge deletions.

value.rationale: Removing a matching is a natural structured perturbation of the biclique and exposes how parity constraints depend on near-complete neighborhoods. The exact class description for all non-saturating sizes gives every palette count and every optimizer. The opposite changes under one deletion in the even/even and odd/odd cases identify a concrete boundary in the behavior of the strong odd chromatic invariant. The contribution is not the previously enumerated undeleted case or numerical tests.
residual_risks: This structurally motivated family does not resolve arbitrary deletion patterns or the case when one side is saturated.
